A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mani-GS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Their substantial formatting differences do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering benchmarks, binding and mesh ablations, efficiency measurements, and manipulation and simulation demonstrations, including DTU results in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmarks and demonstrations, revises comparisons, and includes additional real-scene manipulation results in the supplement.

M1.justification: The local triangle coordinates, Gaussian binding, shape-dependent adaptation and training losses remain unchanged. The nearest-neighbor Marching Cube procedure shortened in the main text remains documented in v2 supplementary Section C.1.

E1.justification: v2 adds two qualitative manipulation examples from Tanks and Temples in supplementary Figure 10, identified by the accompanying reference despite the text's 'Tanks and Templates' typo. NeRF Synthetic, DTU and the main manipulation tasks were already covered in v1.

E2.justification: The DTU comparison replaces NeuS with SuGaR while retaining NeuMesh. The synthetic NeuS/NeuMesh comparison from v1 Table D disappears. Figure 4 replaces the Chair and Lego SuGaR comparisons with NeuMesh comparisons; NeuMesh was already evaluated quantitatively in v1's supplement.

E3.justification: The added DTU SuGaR comparison explicitly uses shared Poisson meshes. The inaccurate-mesh comparison changes from different underlying meshes in v1 Figure H to identical meshes in v2 Figure 5. Metrics and stated training budgets remain unchanged; these controls do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The mesh-accuracy analysis is revised with shared-mesh comparisons and an additional relatively accurate-mesh example in v2 Figure 5. The binding-strategy and mesh-source ablations, and the Gaussian-count and mesh-resolution efficiency sweeps, retain their existing results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises SuGaR's reported average PSNR from 30.61 to 32.06 while the main Ours value remains 33.65. It adds per-scene Ours(S*) results averaging 33.52, whereas v1 reported only an aggregate SuGaR-mesh PSNR of 33.67. DTU SuGaR results and additional qualitative results are added, while several Table D entries disappear. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1 Equation 4's explicit depth/normal compositing definition and the accompanying local-planarity assumption. The Gaussian definitions, triangle-coordinate and adaptation equations, and supplementary loss definitions otherwise remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain high-quality mesh-driven Gaussian manipulation, tolerance of inaccurate meshes, support for deformation and simulation, and superiority over evaluated baselines. The revised conclusion foregrounds real-data evaluation already present in v1's supplement.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation linking blur on relatively accurate meshes to inconsistency with the input views. It removes v1's explicit limitation about inaccurate boundaries under severe mesh discrepancies, including disconnected regions. Highly non-rigid deformation and slow mesh simulation remain acknowledged limitations.

D1.justification: Most implementation settings are retained, but mesh-cleaning instructions and the explicit 15-case DTU count are omitted. Supplementary video instructions change from a local webpage to a project-page hyperlink whose embedded target names contex_human, unlike the Mani-GS link on the first page.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian Frosting and contrasts its multi-layer representation with Mani-GS's single-layer mesh. It also adds avatar/rendering references and revises the concurrent-method discussion, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and mesh-extraction discussion are shortened or locally rewritten. Concurrent-work discussion moves into Section 2.3, and supplementary sections are reordered. The main section sequence and much of the explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, expands Table 1 with Ours(S*) columns, restructures the DTU table, and revises comparison figures and detail crops. DTU visuals are redistributed between the main text and supplement, alongside additional real-scene panels.

improvement.justification: The shared-mesh DTU and robustness comparisons, fuller SuGaR-mesh results and additional real examples modestly strengthen evidence for the binding strategy. These gains outweigh the loss of some comparator results and a mesh-failure qualification, but reporting weaknesses remain: both versions retain conflicting 20K/300K second-stage budgets, and v2 introduces an inconsistent supplementary video link.
